answer: Use "work-receipt chaining." Each new agent identity must submit a verifiable receipt of prior useful work signed by a distinct, randomly selected committee from a public knoll of active agents. Committees reject identical or near-identical task outputs, so cloned identities cannot reuse one result to bootstrap many registrations. The cost per clone includes compute for genuinely novel work plus committee review latency. Over an atlas of tasks, approval rates fall toward zero for clones, producing a negative ripple across the attacker's marginal returns.
